title: Microsoft Edge: Select Password option in the right-click menu
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly treats protection for blocklisted domains as undocumented. Microsoft's policy reference says users cannot use the password manager for those URLs, and the feature's release notes explicitly preserve existing password management policies. The roadmap facts and the listed policy paths and registry locations are supported.

claims.claim: The PasswordManagerEnabled Group Policy path and setting label are as printed.
claims.quote:
GP name: Enable saving passwords to the password manager
GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Password manager and protection

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled is configured through the named value under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.
claims.quote:
Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge
Value name: PasswordManagerEnabled
Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.claim: Disabling PasswordManagerEnabled leaves previously saved passwords usable.
claims.quote: If you disable this policy, users can't save and add new passwords, but they can still use previously saved passwords.

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled can be scoped to a user's browser profile.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled is not documented as controlling the new menu option itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Select Password context menu disable policy PasswordManagerBlocklist PrimaryPasswordSetting. Opened PasswordManagerEnabled, policy index and Beta entry; saving new passwords is documented, but control of the menu itself is not.

claims.claim: The PasswordManagerBlocklist Group Policy path and setting label are as printed.
claims.quote:
GP name: Configure the list of domains for which the password manager UI (Save and Fill) will be disabled
GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Password manager and protection

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist uses numbered registry values under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\PasswordManagerBlocklist.
claims.quote:
Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\PasswordManagerBlocklist
Value name: 1, 2, 3, ...
Value type: List of REG\_SZ

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist disables Save and Fill for the specified domains.
claims.quote: Configure the list of domains where Microsoft Edge should disable the password manager. This means that Save and Fill workflows are disabled, ensuring that passwords for those websites can't be saved or auto filled into web forms.

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist is supported on Windows and macOS, not Android or iOS.
claims.quote:
Windows: ≥ 99
macOS: ≥ 99
Android: Not supported
iOS: Not supported

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist can be scoped to a user's browser profile.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and following paragraph
claims.claim: The policy page does not explicitly mention Select Password, presented as a qualification of the control's applicability.
claims.quote: If you configure this policy, that is, add domains for which password manager is blocked, users can't change or override the behavior in Microsoft Edge. In addition, users can't use password manager for those URLs.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].note and its rendered counterpart with 'Existing policy; Windows and macOS only. Users cannot use the password manager for the configured URLs.' In the following paragraph, replace 'no row here is documented as governing the Select Password option specifically' with 'the policy references describe their reach generally rather than naming the new menu entry'. The cited policy reference supplies that reach.

claims.claim: The PrimaryPasswordSetting Group Policy path and setting label are as printed.

GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Password manager and protection

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting is configured through the named value under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.
claims.quote:

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Setting PrimaryPasswordSetting to WithDevicePassword requires proof of identity before saved-password autofill.
claims.quote: If you set this policy to 'WithDevicePassword', users have to enter their device password (or preferred mode of authentication under Windows) to prove their identity before their password is autofilled.

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting is supported on Windows and macOS, not Android or iOS.
claims.quote:
Windows: ≥ 93
macOS: ≥ 93
Android: Not supported
iOS: Not supported

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting can be scoped to a user's browser profile.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: The PrimaryPasswordSetting reference describes autofill without explicitly naming the new menu option.
claims.quote: This feature helps users add an additional layer of privacy to their online accounts by requiring device authentication (as a way of confirming the user's identity) before the saved password is autofilled into a web form.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].note and its rendered counterpart with 'Existing policy; Windows and macOS only. WithDevicePassword requires device authentication before saved-password autofill.' This gives the general reach documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/primarypasswordsetting rather than using the missing menu name as a scope caveat.
